name: Pink salt
summary: Pink salt, often sold as Himalayan salt, is a rock salt with a pink tint, used to season food. This page lists what people say pink salt does and what writers in ancient Greece and Rome believed; each claim can be checked against the research when you choose.
inIt: A 2020 study bought 31 pink salts in Australia and measured 25 nutrients and non-nutritive minerals in them and in an iodized white table salt. The amount and range of minerals varied widely between pink salts. Flaked, Himalayan-origin and darker-coloured pink salts generally held more minerals. The study did not say what gives the pink colour.
The same study found that more than 30 g of pink salt a day (about 6 teaspoons) would be needed to add a meaningful amount of any nutrient, which would give excessive sodium.
One of the 31 pink salts held lead above Australia's maximum limit (more than 2 mg/kg).
The UK food table (CoFID) does not list pink salt. Its plain table salt has 39,300 mg of sodium per 100 g, so a teaspoon (about 6 g) holds about 2,360 mg of sodium.

lore.who: Ancient Rome (Pliny the Elder, about 77 AD)
lore.belief: Pliny wrote that salt is injurious to the stomach, except that it stimulates the appetite.
lore.note: The ancient writers wrote about salt in general, including coloured salts (Pliny names a deep red salt at Memphis and a purple one at Centuripa). None wrote about modern pink salt by that name.

lore.note: The ancient writers wrote about salt in general, including coloured salts (Pliny names a deep red salt at Memphis and a purple one at Centuripa). None wrote about modern pink salt by that name.

lore.who: Ancient Israel (Book of Ezekiel, about 590 BC)
lore.belief: The prophet Ezekiel, describing an abandoned newborn, lists what was not done for her: the cord was not cut, she was not washed in water, she was 'not rubbed with salt' and not swaddled. Rubbing a newborn with salt is named there as part of ordinary newborn care.

whoShouldBeCareful.with: High blood pressure, or anyone told to limit sodium
whoShouldBeCareful.note: A Cochrane review of 34 trials found that cutting salt by about 4.4 g a day lowered blood pressure by about 4 mm Hg (top number) and 2 mm Hg (bottom number). The Australian pink salt study says pink salt use should stay within the national guideline of under 5 g of salt a day. If you have been told to limit salt, talk to your doctor.

unknowns: Whether pink salt has any health effect different from table salt: the Australian study measured minerals, not health outcomes.
What gives a given pink salt its colour and mineral content: it varies by source and form.
Whether the trace minerals and lead found in some pink salts matter at the amounts a person eats: the study did not test that.
